newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle crew among most diverse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle crew among most diverse.

text.p: The crew of the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis that was to be launched on Thursday is one of NASA's most diverse, including a U.S. woman pilot and a Russian woman cosmonaut, and French, British and Peruvian-born men.

Here are thumbnail biographies of the seven people on board Atlantis for its 10-day mission to supply Russia's Mir space station, pick up U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger after four months on Mir, and leave behind Michael Foale, a NASA astronaut from Cambridge, England.

- Jean-Francois Clervoy, a European Space Agency astronaut from Toulose, France, 38, is the mission's Payload Commander. Selected in the second group of French astronauts in 1985, he reported to the Johnson Space Centre in Houston in August 1992 and was a mission specialist aboard Atlantis on a science mission in November 1994.

- Atlantis's pilot, Eileen Marie Collins, 40, a NASA astronaut and U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel, was the first woman pilot of a space shuttle during her first mission on board the shuttle Discovery in February 1995. An astronaut since 1991, Collins was born in Elmira, New York.
She is married and has one child.

- Foale, 40, was born in Louth, England, but considers Cambridge his hometown. Educated at Cambridge University, he was selected as a NASA astronaut candidate in June 1987. A veteran of three space flights, he has spent more than 643 hours in space, most recently as a mission specialist in February 1995, the first shuttle rendezvous with Mir.
Married with two children, Foale is mission specialist on Atlantis and expected to spend four months aboard Mir. He was to be the fifth NASA astronaut to live on the Russian space outpost.

- Russian Space Agency cosmonaut Elena Kondakova, 40, has spent 169 days in space, with her first flight onboard the spacecraft "Soyuz TM-17" and on board Mir. She will serve as a mission specialist on the Atlantis mission that blasted off Thursday.
Born in Mitischi, Moscow Region, Kondakova is married and has one child.

- Thirty-three-year-old Edward Tsang Lu considers Honolulu, Hawaii, and Webster, New York, to be his hometowns. Unmarried and childless, he was selected by NASA in 1994, and reported to the Johnson Space Centre in March 1995. A mission specialist on board Atlantis, he is making his first trip into space.

- NASA astronaut Carlos Noriega, 37, was born in Lima, Peru, but considers Santa Clara, California, his hometown. He is a major in the U.S. Marine Corps and was selected by NASA in December 1994. A mission specialist on board Atlantis, Noriega is making his first trip into space.
He is married and has five children.

- Charles Precourt, 41, of Hudson, Massachusetts, a U.S. Air Force Colonel, has been a NASA astronaut since July 1991. He is a veteran of two space flights with over 475 hours in space, most recently as pilot on a mission that ended on July 7, 1995.
The commander of Atlantis' mission, Precourt is married and has three children.

Atlantis will bring back to Earth Linenger, 42, a doctor, Navy captain and NASA astronaut who was born and raised in Eastpointe, Michigan. A veteran of one shuttle mission before Atlantis carried him to Mir in January, he is married and has one son and is expecting his second child in June.
